method: Dependency DAG built from the sixteen activation cards in planning/components.json: subsystem edges from the subsystem graph (export-062), external producers (Imago, Nucleus, Golusoris, upstream), toolchain admissions and hardware needs. Milestones are bounded, verifiable states. Each is costed (trivial=1, small=2, medium=4, large=8), scored by the number of milestones it transitively unblocks, and flagged for hardware or unverified cross-repository contracts. Ranking takes the available milestone (all blockers ranked) with the highest (1 + transitive unblocks) / cost, under hard rules: (1) done or purely local work ranks before anything needing hardware or an unverified cross-repository contract; (2) the first cross-repository milestone is stack.md step 2 (M09: pin Imago/Nucleus schemas and test one request/result pair locally), preceded by the Aegis-owned schema authoring (M18); (3) exactly one first component (P06, M02) is promoted end-to-end before any second component; (4) build, boot and release milestones are blocked with the evidence that unblocks them; (5) state=ready iff every blocked_by milestone is done. Ties break toward the milestone with more transitive unblocks, then toward the critical path to the first artifact (M11), then toward milestones without an unverified external contract in their own flags or ancestry, then toward milestones without hardware. blocked_by lists direct blockers only; unblocks is its exact inverse.

evidence: Disclosure, because a milestone that edits its own bar must say so where the bar is judged: three of this milestone's eleven exit criteria were rewritten in planning/roadmap.json during this delivery and before the state moved to done. None is a relaxation. Criterion 4 read 'Toolchain admission: if D14 keeps mkosi validation in Aegis, mkosi is selected through the template matrix at or above the v24 floor before `mkosi summary` runs; otherwise mkosi validation is deferred to the Imago result'; an either/or cannot be judged done, so it now records the branch that was actually taken and the exact pin `mkosi 27` that supersedes the inherited 'mkosi v24+' floor. epics.title: A/B lifecycle state machine

epics.title: Reversible consolidation decision
epics.acceptance: The decision is recorded, and a test shows that a reopened slot still requires a verity match before Bless.

evidence: crates/aegis-janus-lifecycle (D15) is a workspace member with its manifest and the committed Cargo.lock: the P02 A/B candidate lifecycle as a pure state machine over candidate, signature check, delta acquisition, slot swap, watchdog and bless or rollback, plus the D13 reopening. 84 integration tests and 1 doc test pass under `cargo test --locked --all-features -p aegis-janus-lifecycle`, and tests/public_surface.rs fails on any public item no integration test names, sweeping 186 public names. The sweep reads public struct fields and pub static as declarations, not only keyword-introduced items: TraceHeader, TraceLine, DecisionRecord and Citation are all-public-field structs and their 13 field names were outside the sweep until the M15 verification planted an untested pub field and an untested pub static and watched both pass. MINIMUM_SURFACE is set at 180, above the 173 names the keyword arms collect alone, so dropping the field arm again fails the bound

The watchdog boundary REQ-P02-08 asks about is the half-open interval [armed_at, due_at), so expiry is now >= due_at, and the expiry is a property of the deadline rather than of the event that samples it: an on-trial state reads the clock and evaluates the deadline before it dispatches the event, so past due_at every offered event plans RolledBack + Disarm, a Bless included, and the D13 maintenance window is bounded the same way. tests/watchdog_boundary.rs forks one machine and drives copies at due-1, due and due+1 three times over -- Tick on the armed watchdog, Bless on the armed watchdog with no Tick ever offered, and Bless on a reopened maintenance window, again with no Tick -- so each triple differs in the clock reading and in nothing else, and two negative tests show that a late Remeasure and an event the window would otherwise refuse both roll back. The forced rollback is traced under the event that was offered, not under a Tick nobody sent. Before this was fixed the deadline was consulted only for Event::Tick, so a driver that never offered one blessed a candidate whose watchdog had expired: observed at armed_at=1000, due_at=1600, Bless at tick 1000000 returning Ok(Blessed) on the same machine value on which Tick returned RolledBack. The clock is a parameter and never ambient -- Machine::step takes a Clock, StubClock is the only implementation the crate ships, and a clock that steps backwards is refused by a monotonic guard instead of accepted; verified by cargo test --locked --all-features

D13 is recorded and reconciled with the dm-verity requirement: decision::D13_CONSOLIDATION is Closed on reversible structural consolidation with permanent hardening still representable, reconciling REQ-P02-05, REQ-P02-01 and REQ-P16-05 against dispute DSP-27 and citing export-004 15831276a058 and export-011 528da609dab7 by export id and digest prefix only. The register is descriptive and the machine holds the rule: reopening a blessed slot discards the held dm-verity measurement, so a re-bless is refused with VerityUnmeasured until a fresh measurement is reported, and with VerityMismatch when that measurement differs from the signed release by a single nibble; verified by tests/consolidation_decision.rs

The transition trace is designed as the artefact M24 consumes rather than as a log: JSON Lines, one header line naming the release, both slots and the signed root hash, then one record per accepted step with a dense ascending sequence number, every line carrying the schema tag aegis.p02.ab-transition.v1 and a record kind, and no floating point, map ordering, host timestamp or free text anywhere in it. Rendering is a fixed point of Trace::parse, which is what makes expected.render() == observed_text sound in either direction; tests/transition_trace.rs holds the happy path against a golden seven-line rendering byte for byte and refuses a foreign schema tag, a misplaced record kind, a broken sequence, a slot pair that is not an A/B pair, an unknown field, a header whose count was tampered downward, and a body cut short -- the last being the direction a trace is actually lost in: dropping the golden trace's last body line is refused as TraceError::Count { declared: 6, found: 5 } rather than read as the shorter history it looks like. The M15 verification found that only the tampered-header direction had been covered; verified by cargo test --locked --all-features

systemd and sysupdate calls are stubbed structurally rather than by promise: the crate depends only on base16ct, serde, serde_json and thiserror at the versions Cargo.lock already pinned, declares no binary and no build script, and tests/stubbed_effects.rs sweeps all eleven src files with comments stripped for twenty recorded identifiers -- std::process, Command, std::fs, File, OpenOptions, SystemTime, Instant, std::net, std::env, std::io, std::os, std::path, std::thread, env!, option_env!, include!, include_str!, include_bytes!, unsafe and libc -- and finds none. The list is an enumeration and not a quantifier, and the evidence says so: it is not every identifier through which the host could be reached, because no list of identifiers is that. The M15 verification showed it by planting option_env!, std::path::Path::new(..).exists(), std::os::unix::net::UnixStream::connect(..), std::io::Write::flush and std::thread::current() past the earlier fourteen-token list and watching the sweep pass and clippy exit 0; the six tokens that close those five reaches are now on the list, the planted function is kept in the test file as the input the widened list has to catch (re-run against the verifier's plant crate, it now reports all five), and the claim in docs/build/ab-lifecycle.md, CHANGELOG.md and crates/README.md is restated as a regression gate over an enumeration resting on a structural argument -- no unsafe anywhere, no libc, no binary, no build script, four pinned dependencies -- rather than as a proof of purity. SysupdateCall describes the six calls a real implementation would make and StubSysupdate answers them from a script; nothing runs systemd-sysupdate, opens a device, computes a hash, changes a boot order or reboots. Open point, not settled here: sysupdate.d(5) defines a Verify= key that build/sysupdate.d/10-root.transfer does not set, so the signature stage is modelled and is not claimed of the reviewed definition

HISS-03 is recorded as a falsifiable claim rather than an absolute one: a transition allocates nothing because every value the machine holds is Copy and the trace is a fixed [Transition; 32] array, and tests/allocation_bounds.rs binds that to Machine: Copy and to a recorded size bound, so adding a Vec, String or Box anywhere inside the machine stops the test compiling and fails the gate. Measured under a counting global allocator: 0 allocations for Machine::new, for every step kind of the happy path, for the whole happy path taken together, for a refused step, for pending_call, for StubSysupdate::invoke, and for each of the five forced-rollback steps the expired deadline now plans. Rendering and parsing a trace do allocate, they are not the lifecycle path, and the crate documentation says so instead of claiming the crate allocates nowhere

Gates on the pinned Rust 1.98.1 toolchain from rust-toolchain.toml, with no new toolchain and no new third-party dependency: cargo fmt --check, cargo build --locked, cargo test --locked --all-features (295 tests across the workspace, up from 210 before this milestone), cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings and RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --locked --no-deps all exit 0; make verify-all exits 0, carrying the Python preparation tests, tools/verify_preparation.py, make verify-systemd, praetorctl compile-context --verify, praetorctl audit and the workspace crate gate. git status --porcelain Cargo.lock reports the workspace member and nothing else

The milestone was put through an adversarial verification that reproduced each finding in a throwaway probe crate before it was closed and re-ran the probe after. It found one behavioural defect against REQ-P02-08, the first requirement of epic E15-1 -- the watchdog deadline was evaluated only for Event::Tick, so a candidate whose watchdog had expired was still blessed when the driver never offered one, and a reopened slot whose bounded window had closed still accepted Remeasure and Bless -- and three overstated or uncovered claims: a universal claim over what was a fourteen-token deny list, a public-surface sweep blind to public struct fields and pub static, and an evidence sentence claiming coverage of a truncated trace that no test produced. All four are closed above, each with the triples that hold the fix, and the wording of the two overstatements is corrected in the tracked files rather than only widened in the code. The verification is development evidence about the model on one workstation and closes no image, boot, hardware or release gate

epics.acceptance: Positive: an initialized store answers queries. Negative: a query before init fails. Boundary: limits 0 and 101 fail, and 1 and 100 pass.

epics.title: P03 and P15 interface contracts
epics.acceptance: Positive: the descriptors round-trip. Negative: a malformed descriptor is rejected. Boundary: a descriptor at the maximum block count is accepted, and one over is rejected.

evidence: crates/aegis-vulcan and crates/aegis-hestia are workspace members. The root Cargo.toml lists five members written out one per line with no glob, Cargo.lock gains a [[package]] entry for each (serde, serde_json and thiserror only; no new third-party crate is resolved), and `git status --porcelain Cargo.lock` shows the lock modified rather than regenerated. The Rust toolchain admitted at M02 is reused unchanged: `rustup show active-toolchain` prints 1.98.1-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu overridden by rust-toolchain.toml, and neither rust-toolchain.toml nor docs/roadmap/toolchain-admission.md is edited. Both crates are libraries: no [[bin]], publish = false, and [lints] workspace = true so unsafe_code = "forbid" is inherited rather than restated

The scaffold assertions are refusals, not panics (HISS-07). The three P03 assertions become VulcanError::BarMisaligned (BarAddress::new), VulcanError::BarUnmapped (UserSpacePcieDriver::execute_direct_dma) and VulcanError::BlockCountOutOfRange (BlockCount::new); the three P15 assertions become HestiaError::NotInitialised (PgliteVectorStore::query), HestiaError::QueryLimitOutOfRange (QueryLimit::new) and HestiaError::InvalidDmaBufFd (DmaBufFd::new). crates/aegis-vulcan/tests/scaffold_assertions.rs and crates/aegis-hestia/tests/scaffold_assertions.rs enumerate the three each, show every negative case as an ordinary test, and sweep their own src/ for seven aborting constructs -- assert!, assert_eq!, assert_ne!, panic!, unreachable!, .unwrap() and .expect() -- finding none outside comments. Each of the seven is itself checked to be one the sweep reports, against planted text, because a watched list is a gate only where its entries are reachable: the M17 verification planted a reachable unreachable! in library code and the list, the workspace clippy set and the whole suite all passed over it. The workspace now denies clippy::unreachable and clippy::exit as well, so every crate is covered and not only the two carrying this sweep

E17-1 is satisfied in crates/aegis-vulcan. Positive: BarAddress::new(0xf7200000) is accepted and UserSpacePcieDriver::map_bar returns the 16384-byte window (tests/bar_alignment.rs). Negative: 0xf7200001 is refused as BarMisaligned and is not rounded to the nearest page. Boundary: BlockCount::new refuses 0 and 8193 and accepts 8192, whose transfer_bytes is exactly 4 MiB (tests/block_bounds.rs); and RingIndex::LAST.advance() is RingIndex::ZERO at NVME_RING_SIZE 1024, while RingIndex::ZERO.advance() is 1 (tests/ring_index.rs)

E17-2 is satisfied in crates/aegis-hestia/tests/vector_store.rs. Positive: an initialised store answers a query of limit 5 with 5 hits and reports the recorded 256 MB buffer. Negative: the same query on an uninitialised store is NotInitialised and leaves the store uninitialised. Boundary: QueryLimit::new refuses 0 and 101 and accepts 1 and 100, and an initialised store answers at both ends of that range

E17-3 is satisfied across both crates. Positive: WeightStreamDescriptor and MediaIngestDescriptor round-trip through encode_into/decode (crates/aegis-vulcan/tests/contract_weight_stream.rs, contract_media_ingest.rs), and so does OverlayRegistration (crates/aegis-hestia/tests/contract_overlay_registration.rs). Negative: each has a malformed-payload case -- empty text, an empty object, an added unknown field under deny_unknown_fields, and a renamed version tag that decodes as UnknownVersion rather than leniently; the media-ingest schema additionally refuses a misaligned BAR address, and the overlay schema refuses a negative DMA-BUF descriptor and a non-overlay layer. Boundary: a descriptor carrying "blocks":8192 decodes and one carrying 8193 or 0 does not, for both P03 schemas

The DMA-BUF export path is a field of both P03 descriptors, so M25 binds values rather than reshaping a schema. DmaBufExport carries a RenderNode (the DRM minor, 128..=191, rendered as renderD<minor>), a DrmDriver and a ModesetState. The reference profile was probed on this workstation on 2026-09-13: `ls /dev/dri` lists renderD128, renderD129 and renderD130; `readlink -f /sys/class/drm/renderD<n>/device/driver` resolves to nvidia, i915 and amdgpu respectively; `cat /sys/module/nvidia_drm/parameters/modeset` prints Y; `cat /sys/module/amdgpu/parameters/modeset` prints -1; and /sys/module/i915/parameters/modeset is root-readable only, so an unprivileged probe cannot distinguish it from the driver default. Those three readings are REFERENCE_PROFILE_EXPORTS, and crates/aegis-vulcan/tests/dmabuf_export.rs binds each of them into both descriptors and requires all six payloads to round-trip. The tri-state modeset field exists because two of the three readings are a driver default rather than an explicit yes

Decision D09 is applied. The register crates/aegis-hestia/src/decision.rs records the closed decision -- both a Rust crate and a Svelte package, joined by a typed boundary -- with its two sources cited by export id and digest prefix, and keeps the two rejected options representable. The boundary itself is crates/aegis-hestia/src/view.rs: HestiaView is a versioned, bounded, Copy snapshot the crate renders and the package would read. It carries no method, handle or DMA-BUF descriptor, which tests/d09_boundary.rs asserts by serialising a snapshot of a registered surface and requiring the descriptor number to be absent. No Svelte package, manifest, lockfile or accessibility test is added by this milestone and none is claimed; D10 has still to pin the toolchain that would build one

The transports stay stubbed. Neither crate opens a device, maps a window, issues a transfer, starts a store or connects to a compositor. crates/aegis-vulcan/tests/stubbed_effects.rs sweeps the crate's own src/ for 22 named identifiers (memmap2, mmap, MmapOptions, libc, /dev/vfio, /dev/dri, ioctl, cuda, RawFd and the rest) and crates/aegis-hestia/tests/stubbed_effects.rs for 20 (std::fs, postgres, sqlx, wayland, smithay, Command, RawFd and the rest); both fail if one appears outside a comment. These are regression gates over those two named enumerations, not proofs that no effect of any kind is reachable: an identifier that is not on a list is not checked. What narrows the remaining surface is the dependency set, which tests/manifest_hygiene.rs pins to serde, serde_json and thiserror in each crate

HISS-03 is stated as a falsifiable property rather than as an absolute. Every value on a decision path in both crates is Copy, which tests/allocation_bounds.rs enforces by requiring Copy of 17 types in aegis-vulcan and 16 in aegis-hestia -- a Vec, String or Box at any depth stops the file compiling. Decoding is explicitly not claimed to be allocation-free: both files decode a payload whose correlation identifier is spelled with a \u006d JSON escape, which serde_json unescapes into a heap scratch buffer, and assert only that it decodes to the same value. The PgliteVectorStore is Copy only because StoragePath is an inline buffer; the imported scaffold's storage_path was a String

HISS-15 is mechanised per crate. crates/aegis-vulcan/tests/public_surface.rs and crates/aegis-hestia/tests/public_surface.rs require every public name a crate's src/ declares to appear as a whole identifier in some other integration test, and both collect public struct fields and pub static as well as functions, types, variants, trait items and constants. The floors are measured, not guessed: the scanner reports 155 names for aegis-vulcan and 143 for aegis-hestia, of which 25 and 26 respectively come from the field-and-static arm, so the floors are set at 150 and 138. Both figures are asserted rather than stated: each sweep runs the same walk twice, once with that arm and once without, and requires the difference to be exactly 25 or 26 and the keyword-only count -- 130 and 117 -- to be below the floor, so dropping the arm fails the gate

P03 and P15 stay proposals in planning/components.json; neither is activated. Neither crate is the component it is named after: aegis-vulcan maps no BAR and dispatches no DMA, and aegis-hestia runs no store and connects to no compositor, while those effects are what the two subsystems are. P15 additionally cannot be activated at this milestone even in principle: D09 makes it two halves, and verify_candidates() in tools/verify_preparation.py requires every candidate row of an activated component to record a manifest and a lock, which the Svelte half has neither of. E05-1, the SCI arithmetic. `SciEngine::sci_rate` (crates/aegis-tellus/src/sci.rs) is REQ-P13-01's ((E*I)+M)/R and nothing else. Positive: the scaffold's own benchmark inputs, energy 0.0025 kWh at the recorded default intensity 220.0 gCO2eq/kWh and embodied carbon 0.05 gCO2eq over one functional unit, hand-compute to 0.6 and the engine returns it within 1e-12. Negative: a functional-unit count of 0.0, -0.0, -1.0, NaN, an infinity, a subnormal or -f64::MAX falls back to 1.0 and the resulting rate is asserted non-NaN and finite, which is the half a fell_back flag alone does not cover. Boundary: the defer comparison is strict, so 300.0 does not defer, 300.001 does, and the next representable f64 above 300.0 does; the slice table is a fixed array of 16 and the seventeenth push is refused without changing the table

E05-1's finiteness claim is bound to a falsifier rather than asserted. Every input reaches the arithmetic through a validating constructor with a recorded bound, so the largest numerator the admitted domain can produce is 2.000001e9 and the smallest divisor 1e-6; `SciCalculation::as_rate` refuses anything outside 0.0..=MAX_SCI_RATE and crates/aegis-tellus/tests/sci_arithmetic.rs drives it at the extremes of all three bounded inputs and across the nine recorded hostile functional-unit counts. Widening a bound past the point where the division overflows fails that test

E05-2, the Athena lifecycle and Pareto gate. `Lifecycle` (crates/aegis-athena/src/machine.rs) is REQ-P16-01's seven stages, with only Invalidate terminal: Publish accepts a withdrawal, which is REQ-P16-05's reversible maturity gate rather than an oversight. Positive: a candidate at the scaffold's own sample metrics reaches Publish. Negative: breaching each of the four bounds in turn reaches Invalidate and writes exactly one ledger record, and the empty candidate identifier the scaffold guards with assert! does not become a value at all (HISS-07). Boundary: a latency of exactly 1.5 does not clear because the comparison is `< 1.5`, and a retention of exactly 0.99 does clear because that comparison is `>= 0.99`; the asymmetry is the scaffold's and is kept deliberately. REQ-P16-10's 500 ms check budget is enforced rather than reported: exactly 500 is accepted and 501 is refused with the stage unchanged

E05-3, the ledger ported under D02. `CheckpointLedger` (crates/aegis-athena/src/ledger.rs) is generic over `aegis_justitia::LedgerHasher`, the trait M02 created, so the workspace has one hashing boundary and one implementation rather than two. Positive: an eight-record chain re-walks to its head digest. Negative: a record restated with one field changed and its stored digest left alone is detected as LedgerError::DigestMismatch at its sequence number, a sequence gap and a broken link are detected, and a backwards timestamp is refused on append. Boundary: an empty chain verifies as the all-zero genesis link, the first record's previous link is that same value, and the domain tag aegis.athena.checkpoint.v1 differs from the P06 audit domain so a record of one kind cannot be replayed as the other. The three algorithms the sources name are recorded in `register::LEDGER_ALGORITHM`; the code admits SHA-256 only, and no blake3, md5, md-5 or blake2 entry is resolved in Cargo.lock

E05-4, the edge contracts. P16 to P13 is `CandidateSciQuery` and `CandidateSciResponse` (crates/aegis-tellus/src/contracts/sci_query.rs), placed with P13 because the response carries an SCI rate only that crate can bound and because the dependency must run one way; P13 to P07 is `TaskShiftDirective`; P16 to P02 is `PromotionTrigger` (crates/aegis-athena/src/contracts/promotion.rs). Each round-trips through its own encoder and decoder, and each refuses an unknown version tag, an unknown field, a missing field, a renamed field, an out-of-charset identifier, an out-of-range quantity, a wrong edge and a payload past the 4096-byte bound. The M14 audit record is consumed, not redefined: `AuditIntake` decodes through aegis_justitia::SignedAuditRecord, so M14's version, genesis, refusal-reason and unsigned rules apply unchanged, and the one rule this side adds is which recorded decision admits a promotion

E05-4's two boundary cases. The sysupdate call is stubbed: `StubSysupdate` records what it was asked to do and performs nothing, and crates/aegis-athena/tests/stubbed_effects.rs sweeps the library for twenty recorded identifiers across two lists -- seventeen that are a finding anywhere outside a comment, including the OpenOptions call and the SystemTime::now the imported scaffold actually makes, and three that are a finding only outside a string literal because the graph vocabulary records them as data; the two lengths are pinned by the_watched_lists_are_their_recorded_lengths. That is a check over an enumeration and not a proof that no effect is reachable: an identifier nobody wrote down is not checked. A second check that is not an enumeration is held beside it, in both crates: no line of code under src/ names `std::` at all, every use being core::, crate::, serde:: or a workspace crate. no_line_under_src_names_the_standard_library fails when a line does -- verified by planting std::net::UdpSocket::bind and a std::env::var read, each of which the named lists pass. That second check is over the text of src/ and is not a proof over the category either: the standard macro prelude writes to a file descriptor without naming std::, so println!, eprintln!, print!, eprint! and dbg! walk past both sweeps. `print_stdout`, `print_stderr` and `dbg_macro` are denied in [workspace.lints.clippy] for that reason, and a grep for those five macro names over crates/*/src and crates/*/tests returns nothing, so the lints changed no source file. Verified in both directions: with println! planted in crates/aegis-athena/src/pareto.rs and eprintln! planted in crates/aegis-tellus/src/sci.rs, all three sweep tests still pass and clippy exited 0 before the lints were added and 101 after, naming each macro. An empty candidate list is handled explicitly rather than answered: `CandidateSciQuery::validate` returns ContractError::EmptyCandidateList, because an empty rate list and 'no candidate exceeded its bound' are the same bytes to a consumer that does not check, and P16 promotes on that answer

The wattage seam. `WattageSource` (crates/aegis-tellus/src/power.rs) is the boundary between the recorded simulated draw and the measured RAPL delta M21 will substitute; the arithmetic in sci.rs never learns where a number came from, because a source hands back Watts and `EnergyKwh::from_draw` converts a draw held over an interval. The recorded constants are derived transparently from the imported scaffold's simulated per-slice draws: core 20.8 W is its four CPU draws summed, the modelled DRAM figure 5.6 W is its four DRAM draws, and package-0 26.4 W is the two together. Every sample carries a `Provenance`, a test asserts that nothing this milestone produces carries Measured, and every zone's recorded label is pinned in both directions rather than only against Measured

D60 applied, against a measurement rather than against the sentence. `ls -d /sys/class/powercap/*` on this host returns exactly intel-rapl, intel-rapl:0 and intel-rapl:0:0; `cat /sys/class/powercap/*/name` reads package-0 and core; there is no dram and no psys zone; `cat /sys/class/powercap/*/max_energy_range_uj` reads 65532610987 for both; and `ls -l /sys/class/powercap/*/energy_uj` shows mode 0400 root-only, the CVE-2020-8694 mitigation. The seam therefore takes a ZoneList, a source refuses a zone it does not carry with TellusError::ZoneAbsent instead of answering zero, and a `dram` sample is labelled Provenance::Modelled. Two rules decide the label, and the roadmap states both because one does not cover all four arms of SimulatedWattage::recorded. For a zone the profile exposes, the label is the weakest of the figure's ingredients rather than the strongest, so package-0, whose recorded constant folds the modelled DRAM figure into a simulated core constant, is labelled Provenance::Simulated: Simulated ranks below Modelled in the type's ordering, SliceTable::provenance takes the minimum for the same reason, and labelling that sample Modelled would claim more for it than its core half supports. For a zone the profile exposes no counter for, the label is Modelled by D60's definition of that variant whatever figure stands in, which is why psys is Modelled while carrying the same SIMULATED_PACKAGE0_WATTS constant that package-0 carries as Simulated -- the package domain being the only model of the platform domain the scaffold supplies. This is a bound sentence, not an assertion: power_seam.rs::the_recorded_provenance_of_every_zone_is_pinned holds all four arms of SimulatedWattage::recorded, and flipping any one of them in either direction fails it. Both figures are recorded in `register` so M21's rollover boundary has a committed number to test against

Component activation: P13 and P16 deliberately stay `proposal`, on the same judgement M03, M15 and M17 made. crates/aegis-tellus is the SCI rate engine half of REQ-P13-08's mapping and is not the Kepler eBPF telemetry daemon the component is: it compiles, loads and attaches no probe, reads no counter and opens no bus. crates/aegis-athena is the lifecycle, the gate and the chain, and is not the P16 evolution daemon: it runs no candidate, invokes no systemd-sysupdate and writes no file. planning/components.json records each crate as evidence against the component's activation blockers rather than as the component

Scope limit: this milestone is evidence about arithmetic, state machines, a hash chain and payload shapes. Nothing here measures energy, loads an eBPF program, executes a candidate, deploys an update or boots anything, and no native build, image, boot, hardware, accessibility or release gate is closed or claimed.

evidence: D70 applied, and the limit stated where the claim is made: this milestone builds a kernel in Aegis because Nucleus is a scaffold, exactly as D56 keeps image-definition validation here while Imago is a scaffold. What was produced is a bzImage and 19 modules in a build tree outside the repository, plus a guest that read the configuration back. Nothing was packaged, signed, installed, written to a device or published; no bootloader entry exists; no module was loaded on the host. Construction returns to Nucleus, which owns it under docs/integration/stack.md, once Nucleus returns real artifacts against the M09 contract

The source is pinned by version and digest and verified two ways on every run, not once by hand: build/kernel/source.pin.json pins linux-7.2.5 with sha256 55ddf0df8325d9dad96fcff7bd93977d22e3f50af06527572af59b77c7632b78, which is the value the published sha256sums.asc for v7.x lists and the value sha256sum prints for the downloaded tarball; sha256sums.asc itself verifies as 'Good signature' from key B8868C80BA62A1FFFAF5FDA9632D3A06589DA6B1 (Kernel.org checksum autosigner); and `xz -dc linux-7.2.5.tar.xz | gpg --verify linux-7.2.5.tar.sign -` verifies as 'Good signature from "Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>"', primary key 647F28654894E3BD457199BE38DBBDC86092693E. The gate refuses a source whose signature is good but made by a key other than the pinned fingerprint. Neither key is certified by a local trust path, so gpg also prints its usual untrusted-key warning: the pin asserts the fingerprint, not a web of trust

The configuration is a fragment on a named base, never a copied .config. The base is x86_64_defconfig of the pinned source; build/kernel/10-base-support.config and build/kernel/50-aegis-requirement.config are applied in that order by the kernel's own scripts/kconfig/merge_config.sh -m, then resolved with `make olddefconfig`. The produced .config is 5,520 lines and is not tracked

The requirement fragment is generated by the M18 producer rather than written: build/kernel/50-aegis-requirement.config is byte-identical to what KernelRequirement::config_fragment renders from build/kernel-requirement.json, and crates/aegis-fabrica-defs/tests/kernel_fragment.rs fails on a one-byte difference. Two further bindings keep that honest: the fragment assigns exactly the thirteen payload symbols and no others, and 10-base-support.config assigns none of them, so a hand-written file cannot satisfy a schema row while the generated fragment says nothing. Every line of the support fragment names the Kconfig dependency it satisfies, read out of the pinned source: PREEMPT_RT 'depends on EXPERT && ARCH_SUPPORTS_RT && !COMPILE_TEST' in kernel/Kconfig.preempt with ARCH_SUPPORTS_RT selected by arch/x86/Kconfig, so no out-of-tree realtime patch is involved

Build, on the reference profile's 32 threads: `make O=<build>/out/positive -j32 bzImage modules` exits 0 in 69 s from a freshly configured tree and prints 'Kernel: arch/x86/boot/bzImage is ready  (#1)'. The artifacts are a 16,438,272-byte bzImage and 19 modules including vfio.ko, vfio-pci.ko, vfio_iommu_type1.ko, intel_rapl_common.ko and intel_rapl_msr.ko, so the payload's module-state rows are compiled and not only configured. One row is honest about a limit: CONFIG_KVM=m is carried by the produced configuration, which is what the row asks about, but no kvm.ko is built because arch/x86/kvm/Kconfig makes the built module KVM_X86, 'def_tristate KVM if (KVM_INTEL != n || KVM_AMD != n)', and x86_64_defconfig selects neither vendor module

Positive read-back, from inside the guest and not from the build tree: `qemu-system-x86_64 -enable-kvm -cpu max -kernel <bzImage> -initrd <cpio>` boots, and the guest's /init mounts its own /proc and prints 'AEGIS-M26-UNAME-R 7.2.5-aegis-m26', 'AEGIS-M26-UNAME-V #1 SMP PREEMPT_RT Sun Sep 13 18:32:20 CEST 2026' (the build timestamp moves with every rebuild; the release string does not) and the whole of its own /proc/config.gz, which exists because CONFIG_IKCONFIG_PROC is set. Read out of that dump: CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT=y, CONFIG_HZ_1000=y with CONFIG_HZ=1000, CONFIG_SCHED_CLASS_EXT=y, CONFIG_BPF_LSM=y, CONFIG_BPF_SYSCALL=y, CONFIG_DEBUG_INFO_BTF=y, CONFIG_CGROUP_BPF=y, CONFIG_POWERCAP=y, CONFIG_IOMMU_API=y, CONFIG_INTEL_RAPL=m, CONFIG_VFIO=m, CONFIG_VFIO_PCI=m and CONFIG_KVM=m -- all thirteen rows. The guest reports on a second serial line so a kernel printk cannot splice itself into the dump, and then powers itself off through magic SysRq ('reboot: Power down'), so the gate's 180 s deadline is a failure signal rather than the normal exit path

The read-back demonstrably runs on the built artifact. Three claims are checked together: the release the guest reports equals the one this build produced (include/config/kernel.release, 7.2.5-aegis-m26, from CONFIG_LOCALVERSION="-aegis-m26" with LOCALVERSION_AUTO off) and is not the host's 7.2.4-1-cachyos; every requirement row holds in the text the guest printed; and that text is the produced .config byte for byte, all 5,520 lines. Negative: the same check over the reference host's own /proc/config.gz is refused with 'CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT: REQ-P07-01 requires built-in, observed 'n''. Boundary: the host's release through the identity check is refused twice, 'not the built release' and 'the guest reports the host's own release', so a read-back cannot be satisfied by the machine the gate is running on. The two host-side cases are independent units: the boundary one reads only os.uname(), so it runs and is counted even on a kernel that publishes no /proc/config.gz, where the negative one alone is skipped by name, and a run that failed both counts two failures rather than one

Negative and boundary on the configuration itself, each a real kconfig round trip in its own object tree. Appending '# CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT is not set' is refused with 'CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT: REQ-P07-01 requires built-in, observed 'n''. Appending 'CONFIG_VFIO=y' where the schema demands a module is refused with 'CONFIG_VFIO: REQ-P03-06 requires module, observed 'y''. Appending 'CONFIG_BPF_SYSCALL=m' where the schema demands built-in produced the finding this gate exists for: every symbol the payload demands built-in is a bool in the pinned source, so =m is unreachable, and kconfig neither honours the line nor complains -- it resolves the symbol to n. The fragment therefore yields a kernel without the feature rather than one carrying it as a module, and CONFIG_BPF_LSM and CONFIG_SCHED_CLASS_EXT fall with it. All three are refused by name; nothing in the build itself says so

Toolchain admission, every version read back from the tool rather than from memory and every floor taken from the pinned source's own scripts/min-tool-version.sh and Documentation/process/changes.rst: gcc 16.2.1 (floor 8.1.0), ld 2.47 (2.30), make 4.4.1 (4.0), bc 1.08.2 (1.06.95), flex 2.6.4 (2.5.35), bison 3.8.2 (2.0), pahole 1.31 (1.26), tar 1.35 (1.28), bash 5.3.15 (4.2), mount 2.42.3 (2.10), and perl 5.42.2, cpio 2.15, xz 5.8.3, gzip 1.14, gpg 2.4.9 and qemu-system-x86_64 11.1.1 with no floor declared by the source. docs/roadmap/toolchain-admission.md carries the rows and tools/test_kernel_build.py reads that table back: the tool names are compared as sets, and each row's reference value and its Floor cell are compared against the gate's own TOOLCHAIN entry. A row present on one side only, or a floor edited on the page alone, fails make verify-all; both holes were probed, with a phantom ccache row for a tool the gate never runs and with the gcc floor rewritten to 99.0.0 while TOOLCHAIN still said 8.1.0, and each is now a failure. clang 22.1.8 is installed and deliberately not admitted: the gate builds with gcc

Gate placement, stated rather than assumed: the gate is `make verify-kernel` (tools/verify_kernel_build.py, seven cases, no '|| true' anywhere) and make verify-all does NOT invoke it. Reasons recorded on the target itself: a full run downloads 160 MB, extracts 1.4 GB and compiles a kernel (91 s wall on this profile with the source already present), and the CI runner has no kernel toolchain, no /dev/kvm and no emulator, so wiring it in would add a step that can only skip. CI therefore never compiles a kernel and never boots one. What CI does re-run is the binding that matters everywhere: crates/aegis-fabrica-defs/tests/kernel_fragment.rs (7 cases) fails if the tracked fragment stops being what the M18 schema renders, and tools/test_kernel_build.py (30 cases) fails if the pin, the fragments or the recorded toolchain drift apart. A host that cannot run the gate has two outcomes and they are not the same claim. A tool that is missing or below the floor the pinned source declares prints a 'SKIP: ...; the kernel build gate did not run.' line and exits 0 -- observed with pahole off PATH, where make verify-kernel also exits 0 -- so an exit 0 from this target is evidence only when the case lines are above it; that SKIP-exits-0 idiom is the repository's existing convention, shared with verify-systemd and verify-mkosi. A host that has the toolchain but cannot obtain the pinned source, with no network and no cached tarball, instead prints 'FAIL: the gate could not run: ... could not be downloaded' and exits 1 -- observed with a curl that cannot resolve cdn.kernel.org -- because an unverifiable source is a refusal rather than a skip

HISS-02 on the gate's own external commands, counted rather than asserted: an AST sweep over tools/verify_kernel_build.py finds 15 external call sites and 15 of them carry a deadline. Fourteen are run(argv, deadline) or subprocess.run(timeout=...); the fifteenth is the `xz --decompress --stdout` that feeds gpg during signature verification, a subprocess.Popen, which has no timeout parameter at all, so its bound is structural -- a try/finally kills the child on every path out of the body. Without that finally a gpg that exceeds EXTRACT_TIMEOUT raises past the kill and the Popen context manager's own exit waits on the still-running decompressor with no bound. Reproduced with a PATH shim (xz ignoring SIGPIPE and holding for 120 s, gpg replaced by sleep, EXTRACT_TIMEOUT patched to 3 s): the gate's own deadline fired at 3 s, the GateError never surfaced, and the process was still blocked in that context-manager exit, inside an unbounded wait, when an outer timeout killed it 42 s later at exit 124. With the finally in place the same shim fails closed in 3.0 s with 'gpg exceeded its 3s deadline' and leaves no child behind. tools/test_kernel_build.py covers the good-signature, refused-signature and expired-deadline paths

Gates re-run on the reference profile, each exit 0: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked --all-features`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps`, `make verify-all`, `make verify-kernel`, `python3 tools/rank_roadmap.py`, `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_*.py'`, `npx markdownlint-cli2@0.23.2`, `yamllint .`, `flake8 .`, `black --check --line-length 100 tools .config/agent/hooks`, and `git status --porcelain Cargo.lock` empty
